text.p: Priests of the Santeria religion followed by many Cubans predicted on Thursday that 1997 would be blighted by more war, illnesses and poverty.

The religion originally came from Africa, more precisely the Yoruba people of what is now present day Nigeria. It was brought to the Caribbean islands by slaves, mingled with Catholic imagery and given the Spanish term that roughly translated means "worship of the saints."

The Miami-based International Federation of Afro-Cuban Yoruba Religion in its "Olofi" prediction for 1997 said there would be "More robberies than before because of the poverty level. Betrayal of brothers and sisters of the same religion. War between countries."
It said people should fly white flags emblazoned with an elephant to ward off evil spirits. "This should be put at the door of your home".
On Cuba, the predictions were predictable. A terrible year and civil unrest.
The federation's "olofi' for 1994 said many Cubans would "take baths in the ocean". That year more than 30,000 Cubans fled the island by sea.
